lines.text: They are called the Red Devils — a golden generation forged in fire, ranked among the very best on earth, hungry for the crown that has always slipped away. Belgium, brilliant, and burning to finish the story.
But out of West Africa comes the Lion of Teranga — proud, fearless, and crowned kings of a continent. Tonight, the Devil meets the Lion.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode eighty-five. Belgium, versus Senegal. A knockout. Win, or the dream dies right here.
Belgium arrive as giants — a glittering generation with world-class quality. Senegal arrive as the Lions of Teranga, champions of Africa, fast and fearless.
Belgium — the Red Devils. Loaded, ruthless, and desperate to finally lift the prize.
Kevin De Bruyne pulls the strings and wears the armband — the finest passer of his generation. Romelu Lukaku bullies defences and buries chances. And Jeremy Doku is pure electricity.
Youri Tielemans glides the midfield with class and calm. And Amadou Onana wins every battle and starts every attack.
Senegal — the Lions of Teranga. Strong, swift, and utterly without fear of any badge or any name.
Sadio Mane leads the Lions and wears the armband — a big-game king. Nicolas Jackson runs the channels with relentless menace. And Kalidou Koulibaly is a rock who has tamed the very best.
Pape Matar Sarr drives the engine room with fearless energy. And Ismaila Sarr flies down the flank with electric, unplayable pace.
So here is the riddle. Does the Devil finally seize the crown it has chased so long? Or does the Lion of Teranga pounce and drag another giant into the dark?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on a roar from the savanna.
Here is how we see it. Belgium come out sharp and clinical, the quality on show, and they strike the first blow.
The Devil draws first blood. The whole stadium holds its breath.
And it lands. Kevin De Bruyne curls it home, cold and perfect. Belgium lead. The Red Devils are dancing.
But these Lions do not lie down. Senegal surge forward, the noise rising, and the tide begins to turn.
And Nicolas Jackson pounces in the box and levels it, ice-cold. One — one. The Lions are roaring now.
And then, late, the roar. Sadio Mane strikes, the way only the great ones do. Two — one, Senegal. The Lion of Teranga has the lead.
Two — one. Belgium were brilliant, and ruthless, and so nearly there — but the Lions of Teranga found a way, the way champions do.
Our prediction — Senegal two, Belgium one. Mane, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Belgium leave with their heads high — the Devil that lit up the night, undone only by a single roar in the dying minutes.
Senegal march on. The Lions of Teranga, reminding the world that the kings of Africa fear no one.
So you tell me — the Devil, or the Lion? Comment BELGIUM for the Red Devils — comment SENEGAL for the Lions of Teranga.
On the plains of the savanna he has reigned forever — golden, fearless, the heart of a proud nation that calls him their own. Legend eighty-five — the Lion of Teranga, King of the Savanna.
The players write the night. But the Lion carries one truth — greatness is not roaring loudest. It is roaring last, when the whole world has gone quiet.
